newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African financial index roars ahead to new high.
newsitem.headline: S.African financial index roars ahead to new high.

text.p: South Africa's financial index continued its recent rocketing upward run on Monday, climbing to yet another life high on the back of a raft of bullish factors, dealers and analysts said.
By 1200 GMT the all-financial index had jumped 1.14 percent to a new all-time high of 9,728.7, or a gain of 109.4 points -- its fifth new record in the last six trading sessions.

Analysts said the powerful surge came against a broad background of positive influences, but the latest factor to kick start the climb is a brighter outlook for an interest rate cut after a batch of data showed signs the economy is cooling off.
Recently there was a surprise slide in first quarter gross domestic product growth and car sales data for May revealed a sharp year-on-year fall.

But the jewel in the crown was news last week of an unexpected 7.4 billion rand leap in gold and foreign exchange reserves to a record 21.8 billion rand in May, suggesting to some that South Africa has armoury to defend the rand if needed without having to rely on high interest rates.
"The better interest rates outlook has really started things off again in the sector," one dealer said.

The sector is laden with banking stocks at or near their highs. Investec was last at 178.00 rand, two rand off its year best of 180.00 rand, Absa at 29.75 rand, just off a year best of 30.75, and First National Bank at 35.30 rand from a 1997 best of 36 rand last week.
Interest rates aside, a host of other factors are also supporting the sector's advance.
The sector severely underperformed in 1996 when it was hit by a collapse in the rand, two interest rate hikes and worries about the liquidity squeeze in the money market.
"The sector was really undervalued last year and a lot of the firms have now been rerated. We are seeing a reaction to that," one analyst said.
Strong results in both banking and insurance firms in the sector have also buoyed sentiment.
Investec posted headline year diluted earnings per share up 36.3 percent at 572.1 cents, well ahead of market expectations, while rival Absa unveiled 25 percent growth in 1996/97 earnings per share.
These results are in stark contrast to a series of poor figures from South African industrial firms such as clothing group Edgars, pulp and paper firm Sappi and cement group PPC Ltd.

"Industrial companies have been coming out with earnings warnings, while the banks have come out with strong results. The insurance firms have also come out with good figures," said Justin Kretzschmar, analyst at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

The sector has also seen a bout of merger interest on a complex deal between Board of Executors Ltd, NBS Holdings Ltd and Boland Bank Holdings Ltd which will create South Africa's fifth largest banking group.
Other merger stories that have caught the market's eye include a resurfacing of persistent rumours that Nedbank Ltd, or an international investor, may be moving in on a substantial stake in FNB.
Smaller banks Saambou and Fidelity Bank have also been the subject of merger speculation.
But analysts said the sector could be nearing its peak soon as shares are beginning to look pricey.
"The sector is starting to look expensive and it must be at or near its peak. Institutional interest will taper off as they usually only buy when they see value," Kretzschmar said.
